main_text.p: eium & mollicies. Multam enim malitiam docet ociofitas, Ecclesi.33.Ezechiel.16.2.Regum 11. Item, contubernia & colloquia hominum impudicorum, Proverb.7. Ecclesi. 42.Corrumpunt enim bonos mores, colloquia prava,1. Corint.15.Et vetus dictum est, Si juxta claudum habitaveris, discès & ipse claudicare. Dina filia Iacob, non continet se domi suæ, sed evagatur ad alienas mulieres: itaque amittit suam pudicitiam, Genef.34. Præterea oculorum jactus, Ecclesi.9. Iob.31. auditus obscoenarum cantilenarum, contactus externus, impura lectio, & occasio, &c.

Tertium remedium est, ut homo elongetse ab igne luxuriæ, i.à præsentia mulieris, cuius species gladius igneus est, teste Hieron. Hoc remedium docet Paulus 1. Corinth. 6. inquiens: Fugite scortationem. Hoc usus est Joseph, Genef. 39. Item Antiochus tertius, qui cum Dianæ sacerdotem vidisset supra modum eleganti forma, continuo solvit Ephesio[?], veritus ne vis amoris aliquid ipsum facere compelleret, quod phas non esset. At Israelitæ conveniunt cum filiabus Moab. quare primum scortantur cum eis, deinde abducuntur ab ipsis in idolatriam. Et statim sequitur supplicium, quia multa millia in-terficiuntur, Num.25.
Quæritur autem cur fugiendo pugnan-dum sit cum hoc peccato, & cur non possit aliter melius vinci, quàm hac ratione, quem-admodum Ambrosius dicit? Responsio: Quia

page.notes: Page starts mid-sentence: the first word "eium" is a fragment and may be the end of a word such as "ocium"; left as printed. The first line of the page does not carry a clear running head beyond "NVPTIALES.", which is given as NUPTIALES. The word "Ephesio" is printed "Ephefo" and is uncertain. "Regum 11." is printed with two numeral characters; read as printed. The long s is rendered as plain s throughout. "Quia" is underlined in the print; the underline is not reproduced. The line "Ecclesi.9." and the reference numbers are copied as printed.
